Parliament debates Budget 2026

Budget debate24 February 2026 – 26 February 2026 budget-2859, budget-2857, budget-2861, budget-2867

A parliamentary debate on Budget 2026, with MPs speaking and the Prime Minister responding to clarifications.

MPs said Budget 2026 continues one-off support such as CDC vouchers and utilities rebates, and strengthens CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates for seniors. They also said it raises the monthly household income threshold for student care fee assistance to $6,500 and lowers PARF rebates by 45% with a $30,000 cap. The transcript records many further proposals, but does not state that they have been adopted.

What happens next Several Members said they would raise details at the Committee of Supply debates; the Prime Minister said Minister Indranee will share the Government's approach on marriage, procreation, parenthood, adoption and immigration during the COS.

Open questions from this debate (12)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether the Government will adopt the proposed changes to CDC voucher distribution.
  • Whether the $20,000 income tax exemption threshold will be reviewed or adjusted.
  • Whether the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme income threshold will be raised.
  • Whether advance retrenchment notification will be agreed by the tripartite partners.
  • Whether transitional relief will be provided for car buyers affected by the PARF rebate changes.
  • Whether dental care will be integrated into Healthier SG.
  • Whether Personal Learning Devices will be extended to primary school students.
  • Whether estate duty or a Net Annual Value tax will be reintroduced.
  • Whether the Government will commit to annual reporting of AI value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes.
  • Whether adoption leave will be aligned with maternity leave at 16 weeks.
  • Whether the Silver Support per capita household income criterion will be removed or reviewed.
  • Whether the Government will increase subsidies for assisted reproductive treatments.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 70 (complete)
  • Briefs on this page: 1 (28 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 98% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
